overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a cool, marine-influenced morning with temperatures locked in a very narrow range around 62-63°F since midnight, showing essentially zero warming velocity. Overcast skies, patchy fog, and persistent onshore southwest winds are suppressing the typical diurnal warming cycle, keeping conditions well below seasonal norms for late June.
forecast_obs_notes: The NWP models show moderate spread: HRRR is the warmest at 70.3°F, ECMWF at 68.2°F, and NBM most conservative at 67.0°F. However, given that it is already past 7:30 AM local time with zero warming trend and the running max still at 63.0°F, the morning marine layer is running deeper and more persistent than models anticipated, suggesting the afternoon high may come in at or below the lower end of the NWP range.
max_temp_prediction: With no warming signal through 6:52 AM local time and a thick marine layer in place through late morning per NWS forecast, meaningful heating will be compressed into a narrow afternoon window. The NWS official forecast of 69°F appears optimistic given current observations; a high in the 67-69°F range is most likely, but a sub-67°F outcome cannot be ruled out if fog lingers past noon. Best estimate is approximately 68°F, with moderate-low confidence given the flat early morning trend.
